authored_explainer.title: Cereal Production Grew 1.5x Since 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Food fears missed how quickly cereal production grew.
says: From 1985 to 2017, progression to secondary school rose from 77.8% to 91.3% — 1.2 times higher.
From 1972 to 2024, cereal production rose from 1083.7 to 1644.1 million metric tons — 1.5 times higher.
Farmland spans 5.2 million square kilometers in China, 4.2 in the United States, 3.6 Australia, 2.4 Brazil, and 2.2 Russia.
authored_explainer.closing: Food production changed faster than the old shortage warnings expected.
authored_explainer.question: Which shift surprised you most?

authored_explainer.title: Combustible Renewables And Waste Tripled Since 1990
authored_explainer.hook: Waste became a much bigger part of global energy.
says: From 1990 to 2024, combustible renewables and waste rose from 10.2% to 30.1% of energy — 3.0 times higher.
From 1998 to 2024, electricity access rose from 73.2% to 91.9% of population — 1.3 times higher.
From 1972 to 2024, methane (CH4) emissions from waste rose from 903.8 to 1,652 Mt CO2e — 1.8 times higher.
authored_explainer.closing: Turning waste into energy grew, but its methane burden grew too.
authored_explainer.question: Which energy shift surprised you most?

authored_explainer.title: Population Growth Fell 54% Since 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Population growth slowed while cities kept expanding.
says: From 1972 to 2025, rural population fell from 63.1% to 42.2% of total population — down to 67 percent.
From 1972 to 2025, the largest city's share shifted from 18.2% to 16.2% of urban population — barely moved.
From 1972 to 2025, population growth fell from 2 annual % to 0.91 annual % — down to 46 percent.
authored_explainer.closing: The population still grows, but the annual pace is now less than half as fast.
authored_explainer.question: Did you expect growth to slow?
